risks.basis: the same app (tooling) has this defect on record
risks.risk: tools/gh_push.py pushes to origin/main through the GitHub REST API, so git is never invoked and .githooks/pre-push never fires. TWO HOLES, and the second is worse than the first. (1) NO GATE RAN AT ALL on that path: the seed gate, the Tier A independent-review gate, the generated-document check, the tool-inventory check, the conflict-marker check, the redaction and pre-auth-oracle checks -- all fourteen checks in tools/sairn_push_gate_hook.py, plus tools/register_feed_gate.py and tools/hover_auditor_scope_gate.py -- had no effect whatsoever. Audited 2026-09-26 and the premise that something else covered them is FALSE: gh_push.py imports os, sys, json, base64, urllib and gh_token and invokes nothing, so the git hook was never decorative and removing it would have disabled the gate for every ordinary git push. (2) A REST PUSH SENDS WORKING-TREE BYTES, so gh_push.py could publish content that existed in NO local commit, on no branch, in no reflog -- which means even a gate that had run would have had nothing to judge, and a later bisect or review could never see what was shipped. FIXED by INVOKING the hook rather than copying its checks: gh_push.py now runs .githooks/pre-push with exactly the stdin git would have supplied (local ref, local sha, remote ref, remote sha), after a pre-flight that requires every file to be tracked, committed and CLEAN and requires HEAD to descend from the remote tip -- which is what makes remote..HEAD a real range. Copying the checks would have been item 94 on the largest gate on the platform, and a fourth gate added to the hook later would silently not apply to this path. The soundness argument for gating remote..HEAD when the push sends less is written into the code: the pushed tree is the remote's with the named files overwritten by their working-tree bytes, those bytes ARE HEAD's bytes because clean is required, so the push publishes a SUBSET of the range -- over-blocking, never under-blocking. It fails CLOSED (missing hook, no sh on PATH, remote tip absent from the clone) which diverges from the hook's documented fail-open standard on purpose: the hook is the path used for every push and must not be rippable, this is a hand-run bypass where a could-not-tell costs one retry. Held by tests/run_gh_push_gate_probe.py, 9 arms against real throwaway repositories, including a CONTROL that a clean state is allowed and an arm that main() actually CALLS the gate before any GitHub write.
